To: Executive Leadership Team, Supply Chain and Sustainability
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing delivered cost and carbon across our warehouse-to-store network
Date: Today

Context
We operate a distributed network shipping from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Each warehouse-to-store route carries two performance signals: a per‑unit shipping spend and a per‑unit carbon intensity. In practice, the lowest‑cost routes often carry higher emissions, while cleaner options can be more expensive. Balancing these forces is central to protecting margin, meeting customer and regulatory expectations, and staying on track with our sustainability commitments.

Operational realities
- Route activation costs: Placing freight on any new route triggers a one‑time activation expense for contracts, compliance, and dock setup. A route is either used or not; once used, the activation expense is incurred regardless of shipped volume.
- Minimum order quantities: Activated routes must carry at least a defined threshold to justify linehaul and handling; partial loads are not accepted by carriers or sites.
- Supplier limits per store: To manage receiving capacity and vendor complexity, each store may source from no more than a set number of warehouses in any given planning period.

Supply and demand guardrails
- Warehouses have finite inventory positions that we cannot exceed.
- Each store has a required minimum intake that must be met.
- Activated routes must move at least their threshold quantity, and stores may accept deliveries from only a limited number of warehouses.

Management priority
Leadership has set the relative importance of spend versus emissions. We will evaluate shipping plans using a blended score that reflects these priorities: per‑unit variable shipping spend and per‑unit carbon are weighted according to management’s guidance, and route activation expenses are treated at full value (not weighted). This aligns day‑to‑day logistics choices with our sustainability targets without losing sight of total delivered cost.

Business goal
Identify which warehouse‑to‑store routes to activate and how much to ship on each, so that:
- Warehouse inventory is respected
- Every store’s minimum intake is fulfilled
- Any activated route meets its minimum order quantity
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses
- The combined score—weighted variable spend plus weighted emissions, with full route activation expenses included—is as low as possible

Proposed path
- Use the latest lane‑level cost and carbon data to assess all feasible routes.
- Evaluate trade‑offs between marginal cost and marginal emissions while honoring activation fees, minimums, and supplier limits.
- Provide a recommended shipping plan and a short list of near‑equivalent alternatives, highlighting how results shift if leadership adjusts the cost‑versus‑emissions emphasis.
- Embed the final rule set in our transportation planning playbook and cadence the data refresh so the plan remains current.
